text:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT: auroraedge (tenant: auroraedge-prod) - elevated 5xx rate observed on dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2. Start: 2026-02-23T15:20:34Z. Symptom: ~14% 5xx for /v1/generate and chat routes, sporadic latency spikes. Impact: customer UI errors + automated retries. Pager routed to @oncall-sre. Link: https://ops.redwood.example/incident/3329991234 :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: taking this. pinging @raj.kapoor @maria.su and @ccs-alyssa. quick check: any config changes or deployments in the last hour?

ccs-alyssa: customer support confirmed multiple enterprise users reporting timeouts. Customer: AuroraEdge (enterprise, VPC, dedicated pool, pinned model `rwd-7b-v1`). They say failover isn't automatic for them — they rely on our tenant pinning.

maria.su: looking at telemetry — tail logs show a flood of kv-cache-miss warnings and OOM-ish GC pressure on the GPU workers serving the tenant. Model token QPS unchanged. Suspect a hot-prefix causing cache churn.

raj.kapoor: can do tenant-level override. Options: 
- pin tenant to a safe variant we already vetted (`rwd-7b-v1-safe` quantized)
- route tenant traffic to fallback dedicated pool `dedicated-fallback-e3`
- burst to hosted pool (costly, but quick)
Need to surface the customer approval path for model changes.

oncall-sre: proposed immediate plan: 
1) apply a 5% canary tenant pin to `rwd-7b-v1-safe` (fast revert)
2) monitor errors/latency 10m window
3) if good, escalate to 30% -> 100%
4) if fails, shift to hosted fallback and open full SRE incident playbook.
Who can run the pin?

maria.su: I can run it. admin API call lined up: 
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.api/pin" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"tenant":"auroraedge-prod","model":"rwd-7b-v1-safe","mode":"canary","percent":5}'
```
I'll kick off canary now. tagging @ops-bot to start the rollout job.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout job#22431 queued for tenant auroraedge-prod -> applying 5% traffic to `rwd-7b-v1-safe`. ETA ~45s.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: job#22431 started.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: job#22431 success. 5% of traffic now on `rwd-7b-v1-safe`.

maria.su: initial canary metrics: error-rate on canary shard 0.8% (vs 14% baseline), p95 latency down ~350ms. KV cache misses on canary shards reduced. Looks promising.

ccs-alyssa: reached out to AuroraEdge contact for explicit sign-off. Customer reply: "We approve a temporary model switch as long as we get updates every 10m and you keep us in the loop." ETA for formal OK: 6m.

oncall-sre: proceeding to 30% now. @raj.kapoor keep an eye on pool capacity.

raj.kapoor: note — hot-prefix appears to come from a specific evaluation job from AuroraEdge's analytics service. I've throttled the job at the network edge to reduce storm. Also recommending temporary increase of `kv_cache_size` for the tenant from 512MB -> 2GB to stabilize misses. I can apply the config change via infra console.

maria.su: applied KV size bump for auroraedge-prod. command: `infractl tenants update auroraedge-prod --kv-cache 2GB` — propagation expected <30s. Monitoring.

ops-bot: rollout job#22445 started: scale canary to 30%.

ops-bot: rollout job#22445 success. 30% on `rwd-7b-v1-safe`. Error-rate cluster-wide dropping to ~1.2%.

prod-eng: quick note — the safe variant is the same architecture but with int8 quant and slightly different tokenizer handling. We expect small diffs in generation but major improvement in tail stability.

ccs-alyssa: customer confirmed continued approval to proceed to full switchover. They want a post-swap availability window update every 10 minutes.

oncall-sre: ramp to 100% now. will keep paged for next 30m. If anything regresses, revert to pinned version `rwd-7b-v1` and engage rollback playbook.

ops-bot: rollout job#22460 success. AuroraEdge traffic now 100% on `rwd-7b-v1-safe`.

maria.su: current metrics: error-rate 0.9%, p95 latency back to normal baseline. KV miss rate down 92% from peak. No OOMs.

raj.kapoor: leaving long-term mitigations: 1) increase default kv cache for heavy tenants, 2) add hot-prefix detection alert to rule engine, 3) schedule tenant-level traffic shaping for evaluation jobs.

ccs-alyssa: customer message: "Thanks, we're seeing the UI return to normal. Please keep us posted."

oncall-sre: incident mitigated. keeping a tenant-level pin on `rwd-7b-v1-safe` for 24h per customer request. We'll open a postmortem doc — owners: `maria.su` (root cause + mitigations), `raj.kapoor` (infrastructure fixes), `ccs-alyssa` (customer comms). Handoff to @raj.kapoor for monitoring for the next 12h shift.

ops-bot: incident-bot: marking incident 3329991234 as MITIGATED — severity P1 -> P2. Follow-up tasks created: #INC-332999-FU.

maria.su: quick action items for postmortem: capture hot-prefix request IDs, reproduce local cache churn with small repro, validate quantized variant regression tests.

raj.kapoor: noted. will add infra playbook edits (kv default, tenant override runbook).

ccs-alyssa: will prepare customer-facing timeline and send within 2 hours.

oncall-sre: thanks team. leaving brief notes in oncall log and adding a pager entry for the rotation taking over.

incident-bot: automated note: after-action: schedule postmortem review in 48h, link: https://docs.redwood.example/postmortems/3329991234
